I'm a freeware consultant at this point - it's my favorite genre, hands down.

I went ahead and included the shareware ones too, because quite a few at this point have been unlocked by the dev because legacy project.

None of these games win awards for graphics or animation. They all get high marks on fun though.

Robotron Blitz - I'm a sucker for robotron/smashtv games, and I'm also a sucker bastard difficulty games. This one is moderate difficulty, but when you beat it you start back at Lv.1 and all the enemies take 1 more hit to kill, then 2 the next go round, then 3 etc.. Cool game a guy wrote for a competition just for fun and it turned out well.

Crimsonland - Another top down shooter but it's not the straight forward, no frills arcade as Robotron Blitz. Crimsonland has campaign to unlock new guns, survival mode, and even a mode where you can only shoot by typing the word over the encroaching monsters' heads - as an IT goat I love the stupidity of this mode and appreciate that they even wasted their time with a goof mode (the sign of a developer who just likes to develop and enjoys thinking about the players' enjoyment).

Realmz - hard to find all the pieces because old, BUT my favorite RPG of all time. It's old, it's... not janky at all actually, and the static graphic/map/mud thing sans animations leaves it all to your imagination to produce - which is a trait I enjoy about video games, that your mind is free to wonder and create/imagine/interact as you follow the story. Awesome rpg. The different "scenarios" are different stories/quests and while many were made by the developer, a scenario editor was released so the community could make their own stories/items/maps/monsters/bosses - so it got quite nasty in the best of ways. Parties are 100% transferable: items, XP, and all. The game has a "main story" but there are not only side quests, but random "things" that will happen to you, and sometimes these are people approaching you or environmental occurrences, some with multiple branch options. Sorry if you aren't able to find it!

Pendulumania - Look I know what's going to happen. You're going to find it and download it. You're going to play it like twice and then call me a fucking faggot and delete it. But you'll be doing yourself a disservice if you do. This was my "headshot trainer" for when I played FPS. Nobody wants to play anymore when I find the sniper - this game will do that for you - and it's a fucking awesome game.

Ragdoll Masters - Glorious Ragdoll Action. You have no fine control over your character, only a broad control which moves and rotates him. You think it's ridiculous as soon as you load in. You progressively get a little better at controlling your rubber-band ninja. You get good enough to launch yourself across the arena and blindly windmill attack the enemies. Then all of a sudden you are flying through the air, 2 npc ninjas have pinched you on each side and you legit somehow just consciously moved your character's right arm to swing across your body to block a kick from the enemy on the left while also landing a kick on the guy to the right. When you go back and watch the replay you don't understand how you consciously thought about doing it and executing it because the controls are absolutely whack, yet when you stop thinking about the controls you attain a level of control over your character that is so incredibly precise that it makes this the ultimate fighting game. No hadokens though.

Carmageddon - Idk if this is actually freeware atm, but it's hosted lots of places and you can crank it up via dosbox. You race cars, or do demolition derby, or just run over pedestrians in what is one of the most bloody and gruesome gibs I've seen in sprite animations. You win maps by doing either of the 3 objectives, upgrade your car, buy other cars - kill some more people. The tongue in cheek humor was funny for the day - the game features OJ and his bronco for instance. AND it's got some pretty fucking sexy body damage/collision physics for it's age - makes me sad we don't see more destructible/deformable environments in new games.

I got more if you don't like any of these.

Thanks for the list. To add a couple I've enjoyed myself:

  • Free Civ - It's a FOSS clone of civ

  • Open RA - red alert clone

  • Warzone 2100 - Another RTS with early 3d graphics, although I think there are mods to improve it.

  • 0 A.D. - Another RTS, a bit like Age of Empires. This one actually has decent graphics and is still being developed, I think.

  • Super Tux Cart - classic. This used to be installed on all the school computers. We had a great time playing this on LAN with 8 people.

  • Shattered Pixel Dungeon - This is on android and PC. It's a FOSS roguelike and a slightly improved version of regular Pixel Dungeon. It's one of the few mobile games I enjoy.

  • Mindustry - another good FOSS game on android and PC. It's kind of like Factorio, build factories, mine resources, fight.

  • Minetest - FOSS clone of Minecraft, not as much content and mods and a little janky, but can be good, if you mod it right. The base game isn't really so much a game as it is more of a game engine. You are supposed to use mods to add some spice. One amazing thing about mintest though is that it performs really well, especially compared to Minecraft. It's great for low-end laptops with Linux. Also has an android version that works okay.

  • Unciv - Another FOSS clone of civ, but for android. Great for When you want to play some civ on mobile.

That's it from me. I hope there's something new for you in there too.
